evidence.estrutura: Cavell was not a constitutional theorist; her humanitarian career provides no basis for a strong centralization or decentralization position.
evidence.representacao: She was not principally an electoral activist, but her resistance to occupation and service to civilians align more with accountable civic order than autocracy; evidence remains limited.
evidence.poder: Her arrest and execution under military occupation and her aid to those fleeing repression support strong humanitarian limits on coercive state power.
evidence.imigracao: Treating wounded people across nationality lines supports universalist humanitarianism, but not a modern immigration-policy platform.
evidence.diplomacia: Her cross-national nursing and humanitarian ethic favor humane treatment and conflict restraint rather than militarist nationalism.
evidence.intervencao: She aided Allied personnel escaping occupation, so she was not politically neutral toward the conflict; this supports resistance to occupation more than general non-interventionism.
evidence.economia: No meaningful economic ownership doctrine is established.
evidence.religiao: Cavell’s Anglican faith was important personally, but her humanitarian work did not constitute a program for religious government.
evidence.moral: Care across national lines and professional service support humanitarian ethics; broader cultural-policy positions are underdetermined.
evidence.tecnologia: Professional nursing and modern medical organization suggest pragmatic acceptance of applied science, not technological ideology.
